title: CATL restarts Jianxiawo lithium mine, uncertainty remains
gist: Benchmark's satellite imagery from 19 November shows CATL has resumed some mining and flotation/beneficiation activity at its Jianxiawo lithium mine after its revised environmental impact assessment was accepted on 30 October. The visible text is a short paywalled teaser; the continued use of contested tailings facilities keeps the mine's status uncertain.

insights.claim: CATL quickly restarted activities at its Jianxiawo lithium mine after regulators accepted its revised environmental impact assessment on 30 October.
insights.speaker: Luc Braun, Matthew Bird
insights.so_what: Jianxiawo coming back adds lithium supply from China, which matters for lithium price direction.
insights.quote: CATL has rapidly recommenced activities at its Jianxiawo lithium mine following the acceptance of its revised environmental impact assessment of 30 October.

insights.claim: Benchmark's analysis of 19 November satellite imagery of CATL's Jianxiawo lithium mine shows a partial resumption of mining and a re-activation of beneficiation at the mine's flotation plant.
insights.speaker: Luc Braun, Matthew Bird
insights.so_what: Satellite monitoring is an early signal of real supply returning ahead of official output data, so watch it to time lithium supply-side trades.
insights.quote: activities consistent with a resumption of some mining activities

insights.claim: Satellite imagery shows CATL's Jianxiawo lithium mine is still using the tailings facilities that sit at the centre of a years-long dispute over the mine's restart, so its operating status remains uncertain.
insights.speaker: Luc Braun, Matthew Bird
insights.so_what: Tailings questions that remain unresolved leave a risk of another halt, so do not treat Jianxiawo volumes as fully secure in lithium supply models.
insights.quote: continued use of tailings facilities at the heart of the years-long saga around the mine’s resumption of activities
insights.locator: Imagery also shows continued use of tailings

insights.claim: The Jianxiawo lithium mine's licensing changed after its previous lithium byproduct license expired in summer 2025, and the mining license conversion followed in November 2025.
insights.speaker: Luc Braun, Matthew Bird
insights.so_what: The move from a byproduct license to a full mining license shows regulators are tightening their oversight of the mine, and licensing is the main risk that could interrupt its output.
insights.locator: Imagery also shows continued use of tailings
